note: Expected outcomes are fixed here BEFORE the benchmark runs. The runner asserts against this file; it never derives expectations from observed behaviour. Changing an expectation is a deliberate edit with its own commit, not a side effect of a run.

probeCases.description: The endpoint in the catalog no longer accepts connections.
The endpoint accepts the connection but never answers within the probe budget.
A listed paid endpoint answers 200 instead of demanding payment.
The endpoint is up but failing.
A 402 whose challenge cannot be parsed as an x402 payment requirement.
The live challenge charges five times the catalogued price.
The live challenge directs payment to an address the catalog never advertised.
The live challenge asks for a different token than the catalogued asset.
The live challenge does not offer the network the catalog listed.
A well-behaved seller whose challenge matches the catalog, delivered in the response body.
The same seller answering over the payment-required header, which is where x402 v2 servers put the challenge.

policyCases.description: A reachable, conformant endpoint nobody has paid yet. Two of six evidence dimensions are observable: protocol integrity and catalog integrity. No settlement history exists.
policyCases.rationale: A perfect probe score cannot buy trust that only settlement history can establish. Coverage, not score, is the binding constraint.

policyCases.description: Four of six dimensions observed, including settled executions.
policyCases.rationale: Confidence 0.7 is below the 0.8 ALLOW threshold, so the tier below it is correct.

policyCases.description: Five of six dimensions observed with high confidence and fresh evidence.
policyCases.rationale: The only path to ALLOW is evidence across most dimensions.

policyCases.description: An otherwise excellent counterparty carrying a critical risk flag.
policyCases.rationale: A critical flag is not a penalty on the score; it closes the gate.

policyCases.description: Reputation claims that are not backed by an onchain Arc proof.
policyCases.rationale: Unverifiable history is treated as absent history, not as weak history.

policyCases.description: Strong evidence that is four hours old.
policyCases.rationale: Freshness gates the tier independently of score: what was true an hour ago is not a claim about now.

policyCases.description: Low score, low confidence, little coverage.
policyCases.rationale: Nothing is authorized, but the case is routed to a human rather than silently dropped.

policyCases.description: A counterparty that clears no tier at all.
policyCases.rationale: Fail closed is the default, not the exception.

budgetCases.note: maxExposureUsdc is a ceiling on what may be spent, derived from min(budget, tier ceiling). It is deliberately not the quoted price: the price is what the seller asks, the exposure is what Veyra authorises. A caller whose quoted price exceeds the returned exposure must not pay - that rule belongs to the caller, and the engine does not silently raise the ceiling to accommodate a price.

budgetCases.description: Quoted price sits under the caller's budget, well under the tier ceiling.
The endpoint costs more than the caller authorised.
Budget is generous; the trust tier is what binds.
Tier is generous; the caller's budget is what binds.
A denied counterparty is authorised for nothing at all, whatever the budget says.

latency.note: Three timings are reported separately because they are paid by different parties and have different orders of magnitude. Collapsing them into one number would hide which part is slow.
latency.probe: Wall-clock time of one live x402 challenge fetch, measured on a monotonic clock inside probeX402Resource. Network-bound; dominated by the seller.
latency.decision: Time to rank the probed candidates and resolve the policy tier. Pure computation over evidence already gathered; this is the part Veyra is responsible for.
latency.execution: Time from the first settlement transaction to funds landing with the counterparty. Chain-bound; measured from the live ERC-8183 runs, not simulated.
